THE CHOICE: option (a), NOTHING NEW. In the Lucas–Penrose trial (dec:idea-one-domains-proof-used-to-prove-anothers-claim), each bridge from Gödel's theorem to a claim about minds is an ordinary proposition, using the existing unstated-premise statement kind where it fits.

The trial's friction log says whether that was enough. If it was not, (b) a named "models" premise kind or (c) a check for a missing bridge comes back with the trial's evidence. Until then both stay considered.

ADDED 2026-10-22, LATER: THE TRIAL SHOWED (a) IS NOT ENOUGH, and (b) IS CHOSEN. @ajs: "Go with your recommendations (for all the open decisions)."

The Lucas–Penrose trial (design cd9bedc1cb114de6) tried all three ways reflow2 offers to record a translation premise:
- plain: it reads "not delivered", and objections do not reach the step;
- assumed: the conclusion reads conditional, but the premise is IMMUNE to objection, so Penrose's line read "holds" while PT1–PT3 were contested;
- taken_as_given: objections reach the step, but the translations are filed beside Gödel's theorem as stated foundations.
None reads "the conclusion is conditional on this, and contested through it".

So (b) is chosen: a named kind of translation (bridge) premise.
- What rests on it reads conditional on it.
- An objection to it contests every claim that rests on it.
- A reasoning report lists it apart from cited theorems and definitions.

(c), the missing-bridge check, stays considered. It is built in the reflow2 PR that follows phase 7 PR 4.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.

It came out of @ajs's 2026-10-22 brainstorm on combining proofs across domains (dec:idea-one-domains-proof-used-to-prove-anothers-claim). It is the part of that brainstorm that is new for reflow2, not for philosophy.

THE IDEA. Every cross-domain use of a proof has a hidden step: "the philosophical claim P is faithfully modelled by the formal statement F". The theorem proves F. P follows only through that bridge.
- Today the bridge would sit in prose, or be skipped, so the conclusion would read as strong as the theorem.
- If the bridge is a record, then: the theorem stays proven; the conclusion reads no stronger than the bridge; an objection aims at the bridge (req:an-objection-aimed-at-a-step-is-read-against-that-step); and losing the bridge in a what-if leaves the theorem standing while P goes unsupported. That is exactly the shape of the standard objections to Lucas–Penrose, as recalled.

OPTIONS:
(a) NOTHING NEW. Record the bridge as an ordinary proposition (an "unstated premise" statement kind already exists, req:statement-kinds-cover-an-objection-a-reply-an-unstated-premise-and-a-method-rule), and see in a trial whether that is enough.
(b) A NAMED KIND OF PREMISE, "models" or "interprets", that a reasoning report lists apart from cited theorems. A reader could then ask "what translations does this conclusion rest on?" the way it already asks "what axioms?"
(c) A CHECK: a conclusion in one domain that rests on a theorem from another, with no bridge premise between them, is reported as a finding.

PUSHBACK, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
- (a) may well be enough. The rule of this design is that an idea from reading waits for a real use (rule:an-idea-from-reading-waits-for-a-real-use-before-it-is-built). Only a trial would show whether (b) or (c) earns its keep.
- "Domain" is not something reflow2 knows. (c) would need designs or claims to say which field they are in, which is new vocabulary for one check.

SIZE (a finding): (a) costs nothing to build and is tested by any trial in the brainstorm above. (b) is small to moderate: a statement kind plus a reasoning-report section. (c) is moderate, and needs a domain notion first.
